audit.whatIsWrong: Hookshot's cooldown is given as 11 seconds in three places — 'costs her 11+ seconds of vulnerability' (spikes[1]), "Hookshot's 11-second cooldown is the entire game clock" (mid), 'Hookshot is down 11 seconds after every failed engage' (whys[3]) — and whys[1] calls it a 'low level-2 cooldown'.
audit.why: Hookshot is 16/15/14/13/12. It is never 11 seconds at any rank, and at level 2 it is 16 — the longest it will ever be, not a low one. The error understates Teemo's own window, which is the odd part: correcting it makes the advice better, because at levels 4-5 Camille rarely has E above rank 2, so a burnt Hookshot buys 15-16 seconds of free poison kiting rather than 11.
audit.corrected: Hookshot 16/15/14/13/12 — 16s at rank 1. A whiffed engage in the 4-5 window is 15-16 seconds of ownership, not 11.

audit.whatIsWrong: Adaptive Defenses is described as triggering on her targeting you: 'gives her a shield against magic damage at level 1, blunting your first poison trade' (spikes[0]), 'generates a magic shield the moment she targets you' (early), 'magic shield absorbs your first poison auto' (whys[0]).
audit.why: The shield is granted by Camille's own basic attacks ON a champion — she has to land a hit on you to get it. It does not pre-exist, and it cannot absorb 'your first poison auto' because at that point she has not attacked yet. The correction hands Teemo a real interaction the entry never states: Blinding Dart denies the shield, because a blinded basic attack does not land and therefore grants nothing. That turns the blind from a damage-denial tool into a shield-denial tool as well.
audit.corrected: Adaptive Defenses: Camille's basic attacks on champions grant her a shield matched to that champion's damage type. She must land the hit — blind it and she gets no shield.
sources: champ-data/_kits/camille.json — P: 'Basic attacks on champions grant a shield equal to a percentage of Camille's maximum health against their damage type'

audit.whatIsWrong: Tactical Sweep is referred to only as 'her W second hit heals through your DoT'. Its actual geometry is never given.
audit.why: Only the OUTER half of the Tactical Sweep cone slows and heals Camille; the inner half does neither. That inverts the normal instinct to back away from a melee champion's cone — if the sweep is already committed, being close is strictly better than being at its edge. It is also the sole heal in her kit, so it is exactly where Grievous Wounds gets its value, and the entry's own full layer says 'anti-heal stays core' without ever saying off what.
audit.corrected: Tactical Sweep (W), 15s at rank 1: outer half slows and heals her, inner half does neither. Deny the outer band, and time Grievous Wounds to it.
sources: champ-data/_kits/camille.json — W: 'Enemies in the outer half are slowed and take extra damage, while also healing Camille', cooldown 15/14/13/12/11
champ-data/_kits/_missing-interactions.json — teemo vs camille: needs-antiheal, resistances-invalidated, autoreset-burst-tell

audit.whatIsWrong: wants.you[0] says to blind 'the instant she walks up to Q-proc her Precision Protocol'. The two-hit structure of Precision Protocol is never explained.
audit.why: Precision Protocol is a two-part empowered attack, and the second cast deals significantly increased damage only if Camille DELAYS between the two hits. That deliberate pause is a loud, visible tell, and the second hit is the one carrying the true damage. Blinding the first hit wastes the blind on the small half; holding it for the delayed second hit deletes the part that actually kills you. Both hits are basic attacks, so blind works on either — the entry just points the player at the wrong one.
audit.corrected: Precision Protocol: two empowered attacks, and she pauses between them to make the second one hit far harder. Blind the second, delayed hit.
sources: champ-data/_kits/camille.json — Q: 'can be recast for a short period, doing significantly increased bonus damage if Camille delays a period of time between the two attacks', flags autoReset and trueDamage

audit.whatIsWrong: Camille's ultimate is called 'her R hextech cage' throughout and is never named; whys[1] and the full layer's breakdown.cooldowns describe Hookshot's CC as a 'stun'.
audit.why: The ultimate is The Hextech Ultimatum, 475 range on 140/115/90 — a very long cooldown that is worth naming and worth tracking, since a Teemo who survives one R has ninety-plus seconds of freedom. Hookshot's CC is a knockup on landing, not a stun; the distinction matters because they interact differently with the tools players reach for.
audit.corrected: The Hextech Ultimatum (R), 475 range, 140/115/90. Hookshot knocks up on landing.
sources: champ-data/_kits/camille.json — R The Hextech Ultimatum, range 475, cooldown 140/115/90; E 'leaping off and knocking up enemy champions upon landing'

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[2] names the first item 'Liandry's Angueur'.
audit.why: Misspelt and outdated; the full layer's Itemization already reads Liandry's Torment.

The wave plan is genuinely good and specific to this matchup — freeze near tower at 4-5 so she must walk on foot, and stay in the open corridor because Hookshot needs a wall to reach you. That terrain constraint is the correct core of the lane and it is already there. Left untouched.
sources: champ-data/_kits/camille.json — E: 'Camille pulls herself to a wall'

edits.before: At level 1, Camille's Adaptive Defenses passive generates a magic shield the moment she targets you — your first poison auto is partially absorbed and she trades back with her AA-range advantage. Do not try to out-trade her at level 1; last-hit at Q range and let her push the wave. Level 2 changes nothing fundamental: even with Q available, she can use Hookshot to close and gap between your Blind shot and your next auto, eating your poison but landing two unblinded autos. Your real job through Levels 1-3 is to not die, keep the wave under your tower, and wait for her to waste Hookshot on a shroom rather than on you.
edits.after: At level 1 Camille's Adaptive Defenses shield only appears once her own basic attack lands on you — it is not up in advance, so a blinded attack gives her nothing. Even so she matches your range and trades back well, so do not try to out-trade her at level 1; last-hit at Q range and let her push. Level 2 changes little: Hookshot is 16s at rank 1 but still closes the gap between your blind and your next auto, eating poison while landing two unblinded hits. Your job through levels 1-3 is to not die, hold the wave under tower, and wait for her to waste Hookshot on a shroom rather than on you.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 are your ownership window. Q is maxed, shrooms seal both river entrances and the tribush, and Hookshot's 11-second cooldown is the entire game clock — the moment she uses it to engage, pivot W away and dump the full poison kite loop until the cooldown expires, then disengage before it comes back up. Never fight near walls: Hookshot needs a wall to reach you, so stay in the open top lane corridor and she must walk up on foot, into your full shroom net. At level 6 her R hextech cage becomes a kill threat; if she lands Hookshot into a cage you are dead, so shroom the exact wall anchors she prefers and deny the engage angle entirely.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 are your ownership window. Q is maxed, shrooms seal both river entrances and the tribush, and Hookshot at 16s rank 1 is the entire game clock — the moment she engages, pivot W away and dump the full poison kite loop until it resets, then disengage before it returns. Never fight near walls: Hookshot needs a wall to pull to, so stay in the open corridor and she must walk up on foot into your shroom net. Do not stand at the outer edge of her Tactical Sweep cone — that band is the half that slows you and heals her. At 6 The Hextech Ultimatum turns a landed Hookshot into a death sentence.

edits.before: Liandry's first item is your peak — her 2,000-HP pool burns hard enough that two shroom triggers plus your E poison drops her to half before she reaches melee range. Use this window to split-push with shroom-warded flanks and take plates; never group. At Trinity Force and a second item Camille reverses the matchup: her true-damage Precision Protocol ignores your relatively low HP, her W second hit heals through your DoT, and the hextech cage means one Hookshot from off-screen is a death sentence. Play split-push from safe shroom corridors, never let her see you alone without a clear escape route, and concede the 1v1 duel entirely once she hits two items.
edits.after: Liandry's first item is your peak — her HP pool burns hard enough that two shroom triggers plus your E poison drop her to half before she reaches melee range. Split from safe shroom corridors, never be seen alone without an escape route, and concede the 1v1 once she hits two items.

notes: The one flagged suspect name, 'Blinding Shot' in wants.foe[1], was genuine and is fixed. The more damaging errors were numeric and mechanical: Hookshot given as an 11-second cooldown in three places when it is 16/15/14/13/12, and Adaptive Defenses described as a shield Camille simply has rather than one she only gets when her own basic attack connects. That second one matters because it means Blinding Dart denies the shield, which is a reason to blind that the entry never gave. I also added the Tactical Sweep geometry — outer half slows and heals, inner half does neither — which is where the full layer's existing 'anti-heal stays core' line finally has something to point at. Left alone deliberately: the 'her 2,000-HP pool' figure in late, which I cannot verify from the kit files and which is not load-bearing; I reworded around it rather than asserting a different number. Also note the content win array (Camille/Camille/Skill/Teemo/Teemo/Skill/Camille) and the full layer phases sides (Camille/Skill/Teemo/Teemo/Camille/Teemo/Teemo) disagree at four stages, and both give Camille the late game against a 57.33% Teemo win rate over 382 games — same class of problem as the aurora chart, and the same length-band obstacle stops me proposing 'Camille' to 'Teemo'.
